title: Myinsaing Kingdom
capsule: The Myinsaing Kingdom (1297–1314) arose in the power vacuum left by the Mongol destruction of the Pagan Empire in 1287, when three brothers — Athinkhaya, Yazathingyan, and Thihathu — unified the Irrawaddy valley from Tagaung south to Prome under a joint regency, maintaining a puppet king Saw Hnit until Thihathu proclaimed himself king in October 1309. The kingdom's most consequential act was repelling the Second Mongol invasion of 1300–1301, when a Yuan force withdrew without capturing Myinsaing, ending Chinese attempts to subjugate Burma. Athinkhaya died in 1310 and Yazathingyan shortly after; Thihathu founded the successor Pinya Kingdom in February 1313, which then split with the Sagaing Kingdom in 1315 before eventually merging into the Ava Kingdom in 1364.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territory of Myinsaing in the central Irrawaddy valley is established in Burmese chronicles and Mongol records; precise administrative boundaries and the extent of overlordship in peripheral regions are poorly attested.
